title: Top-Level Routing for Multiply-Instantiated Blocks with Topology Hashing
problem: Top-level routing between multiply-instantiated blocks must handle replicated routing paths and find legal solutions when conventional path-searching algorithms fail to handle such scenarios.
motivation: Hierarchical SoC design using multiply-instantiated blocks is essential for managing complexity in modern chip design, requiring effective routing solutions.
method: When the same circuit block repeats on a chip, its routing connections repeat too, creating patterns that confuse conventional path-finding algorithms. This method fingerprints each connection pattern (topology hash) and applies a group maze routing algorithm—a systematic search that explores multiple routing solutions—to find valid paths in cases where conventional algorithms fail.
key_novelty: Using topology hashing to recognize replicated routing patterns, then solving them collectively with a systematic group routing algorithm.
contributions: Topology hashing scheme for net representation in MIB scenarios
Group maze routing framework for handling replicated routing paths
Top-level routing framework demonstrating performance advantages over 2022 contest winners

metrics.other: Performance improvements over MIB-aware top-level router contest 2022 winners
